title: Hero MotoCorp and Indian Government Back Ather Energy With ₹1,200 Crore to Fuel EV Expansion
excerpt: The fundraise brings together strategic, institutional, and founder capital in the first tranche of Ather's ₹2,500 crore post-IPO capital programme.
body:
• Ather Energy has approved a ₹1,200 crore preferential issue, with Hero MotoCorp investing ₹960 crore and the government-backed India-Japan Fund contributing ₹200 crore
  • Co-founders Tarun Mehta and Swapnil Jain are each investing ₹20 crore, signalling continued promoter commitment
  • The fundraise is the first tranche of a broader ₹2,500 crore capital programme approved after Ather's IPO earlier this year
  • Hero MotoCorp's stake will rise from 29.48% to 30.68% on a fully diluted basis following the allotment

The Deal Structure

Bengaluru-based electric two-wheeler maker Ather Energy has approved a ₹1,200 crore preferential issue that brings together its largest shareholder, a government-backed bilateral fund, and its founders. Hero MotoCorp will invest ₹960 crore by subscribing to 76.19 lakh convertible warrants at ₹1,260 per warrant. The India-Japan Fund, managed by the National Investment and Infrastructure Fund (NIIF), will subscribe to 16.26 lakh equity shares at ₹1,230 per share, amounting to ₹200 crore.

Co-founders Tarun Mehta and Swapnil Jain will each invest ₹20 crore through convertible warrants. Warrant subscribers pay 25 percent of the issue price upfront, with the remaining 75 percent due at conversion within 18 months.

Government Signals Confidence in Indian EV

The India-Japan Fund is a $600 million bilateral initiative jointly backed by the Government of India and the Japan Bank for International Cooperation (JBIC). Its participation marks a significant endorsement of Ather's position in India's electric vehicle ecosystem and aligns with the government's broader strategy of supporting high-potential EV manufacturers capable of driving localisation and sustainable mobility.

The investment comes just over a year after Ather's ₹2,981 crore initial public offering and forms the first tranche of a ₹2,500 crore capital-raising programme approved by the board in June. The remaining capital is expected to be raised through a qualified institutional placement.

"The funding reflects growing confidence in India's EV ecosystem, though execution will remain key in a highly competitive market."

— Outlook Business analysis

What the Capital Will Fund

The fresh capital is expected to support several growth priorities. Ather is expanding its manufacturing capacity and retail footprint while investing heavily in research and development. The company has been broadening its product portfolio beyond the premium electric scooter segment, preparing to enter the mass-market category where competition from incumbents like Ola Electric, TVS, and Bajaj is intensifying.

Ather has built in-house capabilities spanning vehicle design, battery technology, software, and charging infrastructure — a vertically integrated approach that differentiates it from many competitors but requires sustained capital investment.

Shifting Landscape of India's EV Market

The investment arrives at a pivotal moment for India's electric two-wheeler market. While EV adoption is accelerating, the competitive landscape has intensified significantly. Companies with deep pockets — from the Tata-backed Ola Electric to legacy automakers like TVS and Bajaj — are pouring resources into the segment.

Following the allotment and full conversion of warrants, Hero MotoCorp's stake in Ather will increase from 29.48 percent to 30.68 percent on a fully diluted basis. The India-Japan Fund's holding will rise from 5.75 percent to 6.02 percent, while the founders' combined stake will dilute marginally from 4.93 percent to 4.85 percent each.

For the diaspora watching India's green mobility transition, Ather represents the kind of deep-tech, founder-led company that could define the next chapter of Indian manufacturing — if it can execute against well-capitalised competitors in a market where the winner-take-most dynamics of electric vehicles reward scale above all.
